products.title: Dinamic Oil RE In-Line Planetary Gearboxes — 1,780 Nm to 198 kNm
products.descriptionShort: Dinamic Oil RE in-line planetary gearboxes, 16 frame sizes, 1,780 Nm to 198 kNm peak torque, ratios 3.48 to 3,164.84:1. Built in Italy and supplied with the maker's documentation. From Indus Hydraulics, authorised Dinamic Oil distributor, UAE.
products.descriptionLong:
The RE range is Dinamic Oil's in-line planetary gearbox: a compact, coaxial drive for mobile, marine, drilling, mining and industrial machines — slewing and travel drives, winches, mixers, conveyors, augers and pipe tensioners. One to four planetary stages give ratios for anything from a direct hydraulic motor drive to a slow-turning electric drive.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Range

16 frame sizes, RE 110 to 8000, with peak output torque (T2max) from 1,780 Nm to 198,000 Nm and reduction ratios from 3.48:1 to 3,164.84:1 in 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 stages. The size table lists each of the 65 stage models with its ratio range and peak torque; the ratio-by-ratio table — output speed, input power and output torque at 750, 900, 1,450 and 2,900 rpm input — is in Dinamic Oil's planetary gearbox catalogue, and we send the page for the model you shortlist.

Inputs, brakes and outputs

  • Inputs: universal ST input for most hydraulic motors, SAE flanges for orbital and axial piston motors, direct electric-motor adapters and male input shafts.
  • Negative multi-disc parking brakes, spring-applied and hydraulically released: F1 (132–608 Nm), F2 (132–608 Nm), F5 (110–818 Nm), F6 (110–1,150 Nm), F8 (1,271–3,051 Nm), F9 (200–1,325 Nm), MD (220–459 Nm).
  • Output supports F, H, H6, N, P, T, T1, TL, TR, TR1 with male splined, cylindrical keyed or female splined shafts; pinion outputs for slewing rings are covered by Dinamic Oil's slewing gearbox range.

Selection

Dinamic Oil rates the range to ISO 6336 (gears) and ISO 281 (bearings). Select on the output torque the application needs times its service factor, then check thermal power, peak torque and the radial and axial loads on the output shaft. The gearboxes ship unpainted and without oil; fill with an EP gear oil of ISO VG 220 to 320 before start-up. Where the transmitted power exceeds the thermal power — common on continuous duty in a hot climate — Dinamic Oil supplies independent oil/water (URO/W) and oil/air (URO/A) cooling units that dissipate up to 50 kW.

faqs.answer: Send the application, the output torque or line pull it must deliver, the output speed or rope speed, the motor you will drive it with (hydraulic displacement and flow, or electric power and speed), the mounting and output you need, the duty or FEM class, and any class approval the job calls for. faqs.question: What does a model number like RE 212 mean?
faqs.answer: The first part is the frame size; the last digit is the number of planetary stages. RE 212 is the RE 210 frame with 2 stages. An L suffix marks the light composition, available for some ratios.

faqs.question: Is T2max the torque to select on?
faqs.answer: No. T2max is the peak torque the gearbox may see occasionally. Select on the continuous output torque the application needs multiplied by its service factor, and keep starting and braking peaks below T2max. The catalogue lists the continuous torque for each ratio and input speed.

faqs.question: Do any RE gearboxes carry a class type approval?
faqs.answer: Yes. DNV type approval TAS00000NE covers the RE 3513 (and RE 3513 HRS) rotating-housing gearbox for shipboard and offshore lifting appliances, valid to March 2030. For other models Dinamic Oil can obtain a project or product certificate from DNV, ABS, Lloyd's Register or Bureau Veritas on request, evaluated case by case.

faqs.question: Can they run in Gulf summer temperatures?
faqs.answer: Dinamic Oil rates its standard units for an ambient temperature up to +40 °C. Above that, or where the unit runs continuously in direct sun, tell us the actual operating temperature: Dinamic Oil recommends synthetic gear oil for very high ambient temperatures and can add an oil cooling unit where the transmitted power exceeds the thermal power.

products.title: Dinamic Oil WD Planetary Winch Drives — 18.1 kNm to 400 kNm FEM Torque
products.descriptionShort: Dinamic Oil WD rotating-case planetary winch drives, 3 or 4 stages, 18.1 kNm to 400 kNm FEM torque, DNV type approved, built in Italy. From Indus Hydraulics, authorised Dinamic Oil distributor, UAE.
products.descriptionLong:
WD winch drives are rotating-case planetary gearboxes that fit inside the winch drum: the fixed flange bolts to the winch frame and the rotating flange drives the drum. Three or four planetary stages carry FEM torques from 18,100 Nm to 400,000 Nm, for offshore and deck cranes, drilling and piling rigs, crawler cranes and pipe-lay winches.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Ratings

The table gives each size's highest FEM torque (T2 FEM, class M5-L2-T5 at 25 rpm, to FEM 1.001) and highest maximum dynamic torque across its ratios, with the ratio range. Torque varies with ratio: the per-ratio values, the bearing ratings of the rotating flange and the flange dimensions are in Dinamic Oil's winch-drive catalogue. For another FEM class, multiply the FEM torque by the catalogue's coefficient c — for example, class L3-T4 at 12 rpm takes 0.90.

Approvals

The three-stage WD 1023 to WD 8003 hold DNV type approval TAS00000YS for shipboard and offshore lifting appliances and SOLAS life-saving appliance winches, valid to November 2029. The four-stage sizes are certified per project.

Selection

Pick the size whose ratio is close to the one the winch needs and whose FEM torque, multiplied by the class coefficient, is above the application torque. Then check the rotating-flange bearing: its static rating must cover the drum load, and its life (Lh10) must meet the FEM class. Peak dynamic and static torques must stay below the table maxima, and for continuous input speeds above 1,500 rpm Dinamic Oil recommends its high-speed brake versions.

Custom builds

For heavier winches Dinamic Oil builds made-to-measure rotating-case drives up to 3,000,000 Nm, in-line or right-angle, with one or several motor inputs. Tell us the torque, ratio and motor arrangement and we will put the request to the factory.

Lubrication and service

Oil bath, ISO VG 220 to 320 EP gear oil, checked and changed from the motor side without unwinding the rope. First change after 150 operating hours, then at the catalogue interval or at least every two years. Standard ambient range −20 °C to +40 °C.

RW winch drives cover the torques below the WD range — from about 7 kNm to 33 kNm FEM — in two-stage builds, whose lower ratios suit electric motors, and three-stage builds for hydraulic motors. Like the WD, the RW is a rotating-case gearbox that mounts inside the drum.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Ratings

The table gives each size's highest FEM torque (T2 FEM, class M5-L2-T5 at 25 rpm, to FEM 1.001) and highest maximum dynamic torque across its ratios, with the ratio range. Torque varies with ratio: the per-ratio values, the bearing ratings of the rotating flange and the flange dimensions are in Dinamic Oil's winch-drive catalogue. For another FEM class, multiply the FEM torque by the catalogue's coefficient c — for example, class L3-T4 at 12 rpm takes 0.90.

Approvals

Selection

Pick the size whose ratio is close to the one the winch needs and whose FEM torque, multiplied by the class coefficient, is above the application torque. Then check the rotating-flange bearing: its static rating must cover the drum load, and its life (Lh10) must meet the FEM class. For heavier winches Dinamic Oil builds made-to-measure rotating-case drives up to 3,000,000 Nm, in-line or right-angle, with one or several motor inputs. Tell us the torque, ratio and motor arrangement and we will put the request to the factory.

Lubrication and service

A WDD motor drum is a WD planetary winch drive already built into its drum, with the outboard support on the other end: the winch builder only designs the frame and adds the motor. Seven sizes, WDD A75 to WDD G300, give first-layer line pulls from 7,500 daN to 30,000 daN (about 7.5 to 30 tonnes) on 18 mm to 32 mm rope, for deck and offshore cranes, crawler cranes and drilling rigs.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Drums and options

Drum length and diameter are made to order above the catalogue minimums, with a smooth drum, standard grooving or Lebus-type grooving. Every accessory of the hydraulic winch range can be fitted — rope tensioner, rotary limit switches, the ELD load detection system and load limiters. Drive

The WDD drums are built on Dinamic Oil's WD planetary winch drives, with their negative multi-disc brake and oil-bath lubrication. The three-stage WD drives hold DNV type approval TAS00000YS; certification of a complete drum is quoted per project.

Choose the drum on the line pull at the layer you lift from. With a reeved hook block, divide the hook load by the number of falls and the reeving efficiency: 10,000 daN on four falls with plain-bearing sheaves needs 10,000 ÷ (4 × 0.93) = 2,690 daN at the drum. NP and NPA winches are Dinamic Oil's most compact hoisting winches: the planetary ring gear and the drum are one part, which keeps them extremely compact. They run on orbit motors at oil flows of 30 to 40 L/min, with a negative multi-disc brake.

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Dinamic Oil distributor and supplies direct from Dinamic Oil's factory in Bomporto, Italy.

Construction

  • Hydraulic motor with a pilot-operated lowering control valve mounted on it, which holds the load and stops it running away on the way down.
  • Negative multi-disc brake — steel and bronze discs, closed by springs, opened by the hoisting pressure — that locks the drum whenever the motor stops.

Classified to UNI ISO 4301/1, mechanism class M4 to M6 (NP), M4 to M5 (NPA). Every winch is load-tested above its rated pull before dispatch.
